definition_description: Planet's Dove satellites: 3U CubeSats flown in flocks whose imagery is branded PlanetScope, giving near-daily images of all land. GCAT files them under the programme Flock (e.g. FLOCK 4J 17, NORAD 100938).
definition_source_quote: By August 2021, Planet had upgraded the constellation by replacing the original Dove satellites

definition_description: Copernicus Sentinel-1: a two-satellite constellation, each satellite carrying a radar that images the Earth's surface in all weather, day and night (e.g. SENTINEL-1D). Matched on the satellite's name.
definition_source_quote: The Copernicus Sentinel-1 mission is designed as a two-satellite constellation.

definition_description: Copernicus Sentinel-2: a constellation of two satellites at 786 km that, together, revisit the same spot on the equator every five days (e.g. SENTINEL-2C). Matched on the satellite's name.
definition_source_quote: As a constellation, the same spot over the equator is revisited every five days, and this is even faster at higher latitudes.

definition_description: Copernicus Sentinel-3: a constellation of two satellites at 814.5 km measuring the Earth's oceans, land, ice and atmosphere (e.g. SENTINEL-3C). Matched on the satellite's name.
definition_source_quote: The Copernicus Sentinel-3 mission is based on a constellation of two satellites, both orbiting Earth at an altitude of 814.5

definition_description: The Sentinels: a family of ESA-built Earth observation satellites for Copernicus, the EU's Earth observation programme. GCAT files them under the programme Sentinel (e.g. SENTINEL-3C, NORAD 100690).
definition_source_quote: ESA has developed a new family of satellites, called Sentinels, specifically for the operational needs of Copernicus.

definition_description: NOAA's Joint Polar Satellite System: polar-orbiting satellites whose global observations are the backbone of weather forecasts. GCAT files them under the programme JPSS (e.g. NOAA 21, NORAD 54234; Suomi NPP).
definition_source_quote: NOAA's Joint Polar Satellite System (JPSS) provides global observations

definition_description: NOAA's Geostationary Operational Environmental Satellites, which NASA builds and launches and NOAA operates. GCAT files them under the programme GOES (e.g. GOES 19, NORAD 60133), including NASA's SMS-1 and SMS-2, which NASA counts as the start of the GOES record.
definition_source_quote: NASA builds and launches the satellites for NOAA, which operates them and distributes their data to users worldwide. | NASA (https://science.nasa.gov/science-research/earth-science/sentinels-in-the-sky-50-years-of-goes-satellite-observations/): GOES-1 (initially called SMS-3)

definition_description: India's regional navigation satellite system (IRNSS, named NavIC), giving position information to users in India and up to 1,500 km beyond its borders. GCAT files its satellites under the programme IRNSS (e.g. NVS-03, NORAD 101228).
definition_source_quote: IRNSS is an independent regional navigation satellite system being developed by India.

definition_description: Japan's satellite positioning system, also called Michibiki, made up mainly of satellites in quasi-zenith orbits that stay high over Japan. GCAT files its satellites under the programme QZSS (e.g. QZS-7, NORAD 100270).
definition_source_quote: QZSS is a Japanese satellite positioning system composed mainly of satellites in quasi-zenith orbits (QZO).

definition_description: BeiDou Satellite-Based Augmentation System: augmentation signals broadcast by three BeiDou-3 geostationary satellites on SBAS PRNs 130, 143 and 144. Matched on the PRN CelesTrak gives in its sbas group (e.g. BEIDOU-3 G1, PRN 130).
definition_source_name: GPS.gov (L1 C/A PRN Code Assignments; Jan 2026 Edition)
definition_source_quote: BDSBAS – BeiDou Satellite-Based Augmentation System | 130 ... BDSBAS (G1) 140 E | 143 ... BDSBAS (G3) 110.5 E | 144 ... BDSBAS (G2) 80 E

definition_description: Michibiki Satellite Augmentation System: Japan's SBAS, broadcast by the Michibiki satellites QZS-3, QZS-6 and QZS-7 on SBAS PRNs 137, 129 and 139 (CelesTrak lists them by their QZSS PRNs instead). Matched on the satellite's name (e.g. QZS-3, NORAD 42917).
definition_source_name: GPS.gov (L1 C/A PRN Code Assignments; Jan 2026 Edition)
definition_source_quote: MSAS – Michibiki Satellite Augmentation System | 129 ... MSAS (QZS-6) 90.5 E | 137 ... MSAS (QZS-3) 127 E | 139 ... MSAS (QZS-7) 175 W
